title: Lemon, Asparagus and Pea Risotto

yield.text: Serves 4 as a main, 6 as a side

items.raw: 1 pound asparagus, woody ends snapped off
Zest of 1 lemon, plus 1–2 tablespoons juice
Salt, pepper, and a few torn mint or basil leaves

steps.text: Cut the tips off and set them aside. Slice the stalks into ½-inch pieces. Put the snapped-off woody ends in the stock.
Bring the stock to a simmer, then keep it just below a simmer on a back burner. Adding cold stock stalls the rice.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter with the oil in a heavy, wide pan over medium heat. Cook the shallot 3 minutes until soft. Add the rice and stir 2 minutes until the edges turn translucent.

Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed. Then add stock a ladle at a time (leaving the asparagus ends behind), stirring often and waiting until each addition is nearly absorbed before adding the next. Keep it at a lively simmer.
After about 12 minutes, stir in the asparagus stalks. At 15 minutes, add the tips and peas. Keep adding stock.
At 18 to 22 minutes total, the rice should be tender with a slight bite at the center, and loose enough to slowly spread when spooned onto a plate.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the remaining butter, the Parmesan, lemon zest, and juice hard for 30 seconds until creamy. Season, scatter the herbs over, and serve at once.

notes.label: Don’t rinse the rice
notes.text: its surface starch is what makes risotto creamy.

notes.label: Serve immediately
notes.text: risotto keeps thickening as it sits. If it stiffens before serving, loosen with a splash of hot stock.

notes.label: Lemon at the end
notes.text: added early, the brightness cooks away. Taste and add more juice just before serving.

notes.label: Leftovers
notes.text: roll cold risotto into balls around a cube of mozzarella, bread them, and fry for arancini.

openQuestion: Whose risotto is this, and is it a spring dinner, Easter, or a side for lamb? Is there anything else that goes in — mint, shrimp, mascarpone?
